title: Red Shift by Alan Garner - Rerun
summary: A 2017 Backlisted episode, rebroadcast this week, in which Erica Wagner and S.F. Said discuss Alan Garner's Red Shift, his fifth novel. They explore its layered, history-haunted storytelling and the strength of its narrative voice.

title: Archive: Frederick Douglass
summary: A 2018 In Our Time archive episode in which Melvyn Bragg and his guests discuss Frederick Douglass. The programme considers his Narrative of the Life, a powerful first-person account.

title: Book Review: ‘Anita Brookner: Art and Life,’ by Hermione Lee
summary: The New York Times reviews Hermione Lee's 'Anita Brookner: Art and Life', a biography that corrects some public perceptions of the novelist's private life. Its pairing of art and life links the novelist's world with painting.

title: Daphnis and Chloe
summary: An appreciative Literary Hub essay on Longus's pastoral romance Daphnis and Chloe. The work opens with a prayer that it will bring pleasure and comfort to lovers, and the essay dwells on its lyrical, musical prose.

title: Van Eyck’s genius, New York auctions, Cosimo de Medici’s wine cooler
source: The Week in Art (The Art Newspaper)
summary: Ben Luke tours Van Eyck: The Portraits at the National Gallery with co-curator Emma Capron. The episode also covers auction-week news, including New York sales and a Cosimo de Medici wine cooler.

title: Seven standout paintings in 'Renoir and Love' | National Gallery
summary: A National Gallery video tour of seven key paintings in the 'Renoir and Love' exhibition. Curators Christopher Riopelle and Chiara Di Stefano lead the way.

title: Van Eyck: The Portraits review – a jewel box of phenomenal death-defeating paintings
summary: A Guardian review of the National Gallery's Van Eyck: The Portraits, which gathers the master's portraits for the first time. It is written in striking, vivid prose and calls the show a jewel box.

title: ‘It’s like the 16th-century version of doomscrolling’: the Book of Miracles may fetch £1m at auction
summary: An exclusive report on a rare sixteenth-century 'Book of Miracles', a set of 167 paintings of apocalyptic omens and extreme weather. It may fetch around £1m at auction, and public institutions have the first chance to bid.

title: La Poupée noire | Documentaire | ARTE
summary: An Arte documentary investigates the doll in James Tissot's 1868 portrait of Émile Gaillard's children. It asks whether the doll stands in for an erased Antillean nurse.

title: Virginia Woolf - Un lieu à soi, une voix pour toutes | ARTE
summary: An Arte discussion in French revisits Virginia Woolf's 1929 essay A Room of One's Own. Contemporary writers, including Marie Darrieussecq and Titiou Lecoq, take part.

title: L'Iran raconté par ses femmes - L'époque du dernier shah - Regarder le documentaire complet
summary: An Arte documentary, Iran as told by its women, covers the era of the last shah. It is built on personal testimony and can be watched in full on arte.tv.

title: Watch The Real Matryoshka: A Documentary by Karime Pindter
summary: The Real Matryoshka is a Disney+ documentary by Karime Pindter. It offers a cultural portrait of the Russian nesting doll.

title: Creative Connections in music and architecture
summary: Start the Week discusses Jonathan Coe's novel Lessons in Harmony, which imagines the friendship between Ravel and Vaughan Williams. The guests also talk about art crossing borders, and about creative connections between music and architecture.

title: The tomb in the mountain
summary: A World Service documentary on the Valley of Cuelgamuros, Franco's granite memorial basilica outside Madrid. It looks at the tens of thousands of war dead buried there and what the monument means.

title: My grandmother was a seal
summary: Jordan Lee Borgman's Aeon essay explores Irish families who believed they were descended from selkies. It considers what these stories reveal about kinship with nature.

title: Dreams of birds
summary: An Aeon video about a physicist trying to revive bird songs lost as bird populations decline. It weaves together science, music and the loss of sound.
